A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same privacy–explainability study despite retitling and restructuring. Their text, equations, tables, figures and included appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and omitted content.

before.justification: v3 reports original chest X-ray and CIFAR-10 experiments, explanation comparisons, representation and sensitivity analyses, and autoencoder anomaly-detection results.

after.justification: v4 retains original classification, explanation-quality and mechanistic results, including CIFAR-10 experiments in Appendix A, and reports revised anomaly-detection results.

M1.justification: Section 9 narrows the hybrid pipeline's output policy. v3 discusses retaining unnoised softmax information for physicians while restricting patients to labels; v4 explicitly withholds prediction vectors and sends physicians only labels and private explanations. The underlying DP-SGD, explainer and LDP mechanisms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The chest X-ray classification data, CIFAR-10 evaluation and non-target chest X-ray anomaly examples are retained. CIFAR-10 moves from Appendix B to Appendix A. The Sharma-to-Patel citation change identifies the same chest X-ray dataset, with the same title and URL.

E2.justification: The same five explainers are evaluated against private and non-private models, and the same four explainers remain in the LDP/SSIM comparison. Expanded discussion of PPXAI methods does not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 9 changes the reported autoencoder rejection threshold from 0.04 to 0.07. The main classification and explanation protocols retain their stated datasets, budgets and metrics. Newly supplied training details do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix A, Figures 8–9, provides paired original and LDP explanation images across three classes and four explainers. These qualitative examples are absent from the supplied v4, which instead refers to supplementary material. The layerwise representation and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain HSIC testing with the gamma approximation, linear/RBF kernels and a 0.05 significance threshold. Neither introduces new repeated-run information, seed reporting, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Anomaly-detection accuracy changes from 94.7% at threshold 0.04 to 94% at threshold 0.07; this is not a same-setting performance decline. Section 6 also changes Saliency/SmoothGrad DS-test success from 'Almost all' to 'All' samples. The classification tables, benchmark curves, dCKA heatmaps and SSIM values are retained, while the illustrated LDP result examples are omitted.

T1.justification: The DP/LDP definitions, Privacy Invariance Score, Localization Assumption and Laplace/pixelization sensitivity construction are mathematically unchanged. The standard explainer formulas move from Appendix C to Appendix B. No new proofs or formal results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: the LA/PIS framework, poor agreement of explanations across private and non-private models, the representation/sensitivity explanation, and the hybrid LDP pipeline.

C2.justification: Section 9 substantially qualifies the pipeline's applicability: v4 explicitly acknowledges residual privacy risk from labels, rejection of prediction-vector disclosure, and incompatibility with applications requiring those vectors, replacing v3's broadly reassuring account. Section 5.3 also reframes perturbation-based explainers' suitability for DP models as an open question rather than categorical inappropriateness. The explicit fairness exclusion in v3's limitations section disappears.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies batch size 128, learning rate 0.001, delta 0.001, ImageNet initialization and Opacus use. Epoch counts and GroupNorm choices are largely relocated disclosures. Conversely, v3's explicit 0.5 PIS comparison baseline and general code-release promise are omitted; hardware, software versions and reported computational time remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 10 substantially refocuses the research positioning, cutting broad PPML/XAI background while expanding descriptions of PPXAI methods and contrasts with earlier privacy–explainability studies. The rationale for excluding PPXAI changes from limited adoption/evaluation to explicit orthogonality. Added works include Yang et al. (2022), Shokri et al. (2017) and Janizek et al. (2021).

P1.justification: There is extensive condensation and rewriting across the evaluation discussion, experimental setup, LDP explanation and related-work sections. The title changes, Section 4.4 is merged into the similarity discussion, training details move into Appendix C, and the standalone limitations section is removed.

P2.justification: v4 adopts different typography and a denser, wider layout. The first two benchmark figures are reordered and placed together, existing SSIM and privacy-comparison tables receive numbered captions, and appendix figures are rearranged. The two qualitative explanation plates from v3 are omitted.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through concrete training disclosures in Appendix C and a more candid account of the hybrid pipeline's privacy compromises and applicability limits in Section 9. The condensed organization also reduces repetition. These gains are limited by the loss of the included qualitative LDP examples and explicit PIS cutoff, and the main empirical support is essentially unchanged. Overall, the clearer documentation and qualifications provide a modest net improvement.
